events.p: South Pacific, near the southern Cook Islands
events.sum: Wati was an early-season South Pacific storm that reached about 45 kt near the southern Cook Islands around 19 Oct; no significant impacts were reported.

events.p: South-west Indian Ocean, north of Madagascar
events.sum: Agueda opened an unusually early 2026–27 south-west Indian Ocean season, reaching about 50 kt over open water north of Madagascar. Local forecasters saw no threat to Mayotte.

events.p: 191 km ENE of Nagqu, Tibet, China
events.sum: A shallow M7.0 earthquake struck Baqen County in Nagqu, Xizang (Tibet), late on 22 October local time, followed by several M5 aftershocks. Official figures put the toll at 16 dead and 65 injured, with more than 12,000 residents evacuated and 339 homes destroyed; rail services on the Qinghai–Xizang line resumed at reduced speed. GDACS issued a red alert and USGS PAGER an orange one.
events.deaths: 16 dead; 76 injured (Xinhua, 23 Oct); 12,489 people evacuated; 339 homes destroyed

econ.v: No published estimate. USGS PAGER issued an orange alert, a band that corresponds to USD 100 million–1 billion in losses or 100–999 deaths

ins.v: No estimate published; insurance penetration in the area is very low

events.p: Paris, Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Nice and other cities
events.sum: Protests over living costs and public services turned into rioting, looting and arson on 17–18 Oct, with more than 2,400 arrests and nearly 1,000 police officers hurt. More than 1,500 buildings were damaged (some counts approach 3,000), including Limoges city hall. For insurers this is a strikes, riots and civil commotion (SRCC) loss, with five départements holding about 45% of the damaged properties.

econ.v: About €1.1 billion (high scenario; €309–613 million in lower scenarios), excluding policing and judicial costs

ins.v: About €804 million (insurers' share of IFRAP high scenario)

mr.nt: PM On Saturday, October 24, 2026 — one week after the major outbreak of violence — France held a second nationwide day of protests, with authorities deploying 70,000 police officers and gendarmes nationwide, 10,000 more than the previous weekend.

events.p: Landfall near Destin, Florida Panhandle, USA
events.sum: Isaias came ashore near Destin on the evening of 9 Oct (local time) as a Category 2 hurricane. Falling trees, debris and roof-cover loss caused most damage across the Florida Panhandle, especially Santa Rosa and Escambia counties; aerial surveys counted about 17,900 damaged structures in Florida, Alabama and Mississippi. Wind drives the bulk of the insured loss.

ins.v: About USD 3 billion (privately insured wind and surge)
USD 582 million in reported claims (46,509 claims, Florida only, as of 15 Oct)

events.p: 12 km WSW of Pitaloza Arriba, southern Panama
events.sum: The strongest quake in the sequence hit southern Panama on 9 Oct, followed by M6.6, M6.0 and M6.1 aftershocks over four days. Homes, schools, clinics, churches and bridges were damaged across nine provinces, with Moody's RMS reporting more than 11,000 homes affected; Panama declared a state of emergency.

econ.v: No published estimate. USGS PAGER issued an orange alert (USD 100 million–1 billion band or 100–999 deaths)

ins.v: Not published; Verisk provided modeling event IDs only
USD 17.4 million parametric payout from CCRIF SPC to Panama's government

mr.nt: Active event report: more than 11,000 homes affected plus hundreds of schools, clinics, churches and public buildings; shaking felt in Costa Rica and Colombia

events.p: Offshore west coast of Mexico (Guerrero to Jalisco)
events.sum: Simon reached major-hurricane strength but stayed offshore as it passed Mexico's Pacific coast on 11 Oct, dissipating on 16 Oct.

mr.nt: No longer on Moody's RMS event response list

events.p: Baja California and Mexico's Pacific coast
events.sum: Polo affected Baja California and the Pacific coast of Mexico on 28–29 Sep.

events.p: Pacific coast of Japan incl. Tokyo
events.sum: Dujuan brushed Japan's Pacific coast on 21 Sep, bringing heavy rain and flooding to the Tokyo area.

events.p: Near Niʻihau and Kauaʻi, Hawaiʻi, USA
events.sum: Lowell passed close to Niʻihau and Kauaʻi on 8 Sep, the second hurricane threat to Hawaiʻi within a month.

events.p: Zhejiang province, China
events.sum: Saudel made landfall in Zhejiang on 28 Aug.

events.p: Hawaiʻi Island (Big Island) and Oʻahu, USA
events.sum: Lala skirted the Big Island on 15 Aug without making landfall but dropped up to 43 inches of rain. About 100 homes were damaged or washed away, six bridges and roads were destroyed or badly damaged, part of a highway collapsed and some 200,000 customers lost power.

events.p: Off Flores, 68 km NNW of Ende, Indonesia
events.sum: A shallow (~10 km) M7.7 quake struck off Flores Island on 15 Aug, damaging more than 1,300 homes and displacing thousands.

events.p: Northern Venezuela: La Guaira, Caracas, Carabobo
events.sum: Two large quakes struck a minute apart on the evening of 24 Jun, the stronger being Venezuela's biggest since 1900. Buildings collapsed in Caracas and La Guaira; over 850 buildings were damaged and 190 collapsed, and more than 23,500 people moved into camps. It is the deadliest catastrophe of 2026 so far.

econ.v: USD 6.7 billion direct physical damage (~6% of GDP)

ins.v: Not published; insurance penetration is low

events.p: Central & eastern USA incl. Illinois and Indiana
events.sum: A week-long outbreak of tornadoes, hail and damaging winds from 23 to 29 Apr, part of a severe-storm season that cost US insurers about USD 27 billion in the first half of 2026.

econ.v: Not published separately (H1 2026 US SCS total: USD 34 billion)

events.p: Portugal (Leiria landfall), Spain, Morocco and the Mediterranean
events.sum: Kristin made landfall in Portugal's Leiria district on the night of 28 Jan, becoming Portugal's costliest windstorm on record, with flooding driving much of the loss across Iberia.

econ.v: More than €7.2 billion (Portugal €6 bn+, Spain ~€1.2 bn)

events.p: Eastern & southern USA, Texas to Massachusetts
events.sum: Fern brought freezing rain, heavy snow and severe thunderstorms across much of the eastern and southern US from 23 to 26 Jan. Freezing (burst pipes, ice) drives most of the insured damage.

events.p: Off NW Espiritu Santo, Vanuatu
events.sum: A vigorous swarm of more than 25 M4.5+ quakes began on 19 Oct about 200 km off Espiritu Santo, peaking with an M6.3 on 20 Oct. GDACS rated the largest shocks green.

events.p: 76 km NE of Ozernovskiy, Kamchatka, Russia
events.sum: An intermediate-depth (135 km) quake beneath southern Kamchatka; depth limited the shaking and no damage was reported.

events.p: Central Mid-Atlantic Ridge
events.sum: Two strong quakes on the remote Mid-Atlantic Ridge on 13 Oct; far from land, no impact.

events.p: 48 km WNW of Khuzdar, Balochistan, Pakistan
events.sum: A shallow quake in Balochistan; USGS PAGER issued a yellow alert, meaning some damage and casualties were possible.

events.p: Indonesia
events.sum: Activity at Anak Krakatau picked up in early October, with small ash emissions, sulfur dioxide output up to about 238 tonnes a day and nine eruptive events on 9 October. The alert stays at Level 3 of 4.

events.p: Japan
events.sum: Minamidake crater at Sakurajima produced fifteen eruptive events in early October, sending ash 1–1.6 km above the crater. The alert remains at Level 3 of 5, restricting access near the summit.

events.p: Alaska, USA
events.sum: Slow lava effusion continues to feed a thick flow filling the summit crater, which is creeping south-east, with small earthquakes and rockfalls. The Alaska Volcano Observatory keeps the volcano at Watch / Aviation Orange.

events.p: Hawaiʻi, USA
events.sum: Episodic lava fountaining continues inside Halemaʻumaʻu crater, with a vigorous episode on 13 October, the strongest since late September. Activity is confined to the summit caldera in Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park; the alert is Watch / Aviation Orange.

events.p: Indonesia
events.sum: Lava avalanches from Merapi's growing dome run up to about 2 km down south-west and south flank drainages several times a day. The alert stays at Level 3 of 4, with exclusion zones in place.

events.p: Peru
events.sum: Sabancaya continues to vent gas and steam up to about 800 m with sulfur dioxide averaging roughly 865 tonnes a day, though no explosions were recorded in the latest week. The alert remains Orange.

events.p: Indonesia
events.sum: Semeru keeps producing daily eruptive events with grey ash plumes 300–1,000 m above the summit. The alert remains at Level 3 of 4, with restrictions along the south-east flank drainages.

events.p: Russia
events.sum: Lava domes on the north crater floor of Young Sheveluch keep growing, with ongoing effusion and periodic explosions that pose an ash hazard to aviation. The aviation color code stays Orange.

events.p: Eastern Pacific, south of Mexico
events.sum: Vance formed in the eastern Pacific well south of Mexico on 21 Oct and reached hurricane strength while still offshore. Forecasts call for rapid intensification to about Category 3 before it weakens on approach to Mexico's west-central coast.

mr.nt: Listed on Moody's RMS Event Response

events.p: Offshore Jalisco and Colima, Mexico
events.sum: Trudy peaked as a Category 2 hurricane on 17–18 Oct but stayed offshore of west-central Mexico, causing only minor local impacts and no confirmed building damage. It weakened to a depression by 20 Oct.

mr.nt: Dropped from Moody's RMS event response list; minor impacts only

events.p: North Atlantic south of Nantucket; southern New England and Nova Scotia
events.sum: Josephine formed off the US Mid-Atlantic coast on 21 Oct and tracked north-east south of Nantucket, bringing coastal flooding and large swells to southern New England and Nova Scotia. It was expected to become a powerful post-tropical low by 23 Oct. GDACS estimated about 7.5 million people in tropical-storm-force winds.

mr.nt: Listed on Moody's RMS Event Response

events.p: Guam & Northern Mariana Islands; off eastern Taiwan; eastern China; Ryukyu Islands and Kyushu, Japan
events.sum: Champi peaked as a Category 5-equivalent super typhoon, the year's strongest storm, after passing south of Guam on 17–18 October, where homes were damaged and power was cut. On 23 October it skirted eastern Taiwan, where one person died, around 170 were hurt, roughly 77,500 households briefly lost power and roads were damaged; it is forecast to approach eastern China on 24 October.
events.deaths: 1 dead and about 170 injured in Taiwan (UPI, 23 Oct)

ins.v: Not yet estimated; Moody's RMS is tracking the event

mr.nt: Listed on Moody's RMS Event Response
